---
title: "Hospital length of stay"
description: "How BNR summarises hospital stay following a registered CVD event."
---

Length of stay is the number of hospital days between admission and the end of an eligible admission linked to a registered CVD event. A same-day admission and discharge counts as one day.

## At a glance

| Element | Description |
|---|---|
| **Question answered** | How long did eligible CVD admissions last? |
| **Calculation** | Hospital end date minus admission date; same-day stays count as one day |
| **Reported as** | Usually median days and interquartile range |
| **Related measure** | Total bed-days |
| **Unit** | Hospital admission linked to a CVD event |

## What does this measure tell us?

Length of stay describes hospital use following CVD events. The median describes the middle stay and is usually more representative than the mean when a small number of admissions are unusually long.

## How do we calculate it?

For admission \(i\):

$$
\text{Length of stay}_i = \max(1, \text{hospital end date}_i - \text{admission date}_i)
$$

Total bed-days are obtained by adding lengths of stay across eligible admissions. BNR may also report the 25th and 75th percentiles, which enclose the middle half of observed stays.

## What is included and excluded?

The measure includes completed hospital-registered CVD events with valid admission and hospital-end dates. For an admission ending in discharge, the hospital-end date is the recorded discharge date. For an admission ending in death, it is the recorded date of death. Same-day stays are recorded as one hospital day.

Death-certificate-only records, missing required dates and end dates before admission are excluded. Where the recorded discharge status is missing, BNR applies its established date-of-death inference rule to identify likely alive and likely in-hospital death outcomes. Unusually long stays are flagged for review at 60 days and priority review at 90 days, but a confirmed value is not excluded simply because it is extreme.

## Worked example

For five fictional stays of 1, 2, 3, 5 and 14 days, the median is **3 days**. The 14-day stay affects the mean more strongly than the median.

If all five stays are eligible, total bed-days are:

$$
1 + 2 + 3 + 5 + 14 = 25\text{ bed-days}
$$

## How should it be interpreted?

A change in length of stay can reflect clinical need, pathways of care, discharge arrangements, survival, bed availability or recording practice. It should not be interpreted as a direct measure of quality without this context.

## Things to bear in mind

- Median stay and total bed-days answer different questions.
- A shorter stay is not necessarily a better outcome.
- Comparisons may be affected by event mix, survival and discharge pathways.
- Invalid or incomplete dates reduce the eligible denominator.
